ядра.ядро_en: Be hyper-specific: the more detail you provide, the more control you have; describe the scene in rich detail — the more detail you add, the closer the image will be to what you imagined.

оговорки.текст_en: Model pages (all Gemini Image models): the models "respond effectively and efficiently to even the most detailed prompts" — long detailed prompts are supported.
pro (Gemini app tips): "While simple prompts still work, achieving professional results requires more specific instructions."
nb25 (Gemini app, 2025-10): "Instead of needing specific, lengthy prompts, you can give Nano Banana simple, conversational instructions." — a possibility, not a ban on detail.

nb25 restoration pipeline: craft a prompt "generic enough (to cover most use cases) but also specific enough"; a generic instruction ("clean up all physical artifacts") could be made more specific to remove more or fewer artifacts.
nb25: an under-specified key-value prompt "is not fully stable and can generate less optimal results (it would benefit from being more precise)".
lite: what is described precisely (or visible in references) stays stable across runs; under-described parts vary — see core on open/closed prompts.
Be specific about the subject: "Who or what is in the image? Be specific." (pro blog).
For NB2/Pro (Cloud guide) specificity is named along three axes: 'Provide concrete details on subject, lighting, and composition.'

The Nano Banana 2 page in the Gemini app frames the benefit as instruction-following accuracy: 'Prompts should include as many specifics as you can think of'; 'The more details you provide, the better Gemini is at following your instructions.'

For the first request in the Gemini app (nb25): 'Simply type a detailed description of the image you want to generate'; 'The more specific and descriptive your prompt is, the closer the result will be to what you envision.'
The Pro guide repeats the demand for specificity many times: 'Be specific', 'more specific instructions', 'clearly state' the text, 'clearly define the role' of each reference.

General Gemini advice ('Generally the more detail the prompt has, the better' - Workspace; 'provide it with clear and specific instructions' - Gemini API) is not directly tied to image generation; for images it applies by extension.

приёмы.текст_en: Replace a generic noun with a description: instead of "fantasy armor", describe it: "ornate elven plate armor, etched with silver leaf patterns, with a high collar and pauldrons shaped like falcon wings."
"Think about what you want to see – the characters, the setting, and the overall feel."
List unique distinguishing features with colour and side ("a green left eye and a blue right one and red patches on his face") — they later serve as a consistency check in edits.
The 'before/after' pair on the NB2 page: exactly the missing attributes are added to the base prompt - the subject's age, the action and the place.
Short and detailed versions of the same prompt: the detailed one adds the image type (photorealistic image), a refined attribute, the place and the shot size.
A vague name is replaced by an expanded one: epithet + style/culture + object type + finish/material + specific parts with their shape.
The subject is given a set of stable distinguishing features (size, glow, shape of parts; eye colour, patches) - they can later be preserved and checked during edits.

ядра.ситуация_в_промпте: The prompt is short or generic ('armor', 'logo', 'cat') while the client needs a specific look; the result comes out 'wrong' or different every time. / The image description in the task is general: only the object or genre is named, with no subject appearance, action, place, light or shot size; the author wants to control the result rather than get 'something on the topic'.
ядра.не_применяется_когда: When deliberate freedom for the model is wanted (an open prompt for variety) or one prompt pipeline serves many different inputs, where extra specificity would break the general case. / When the task is to let the model fill in the scene itself from a simple concept or world knowledge; editing a finished image (only the change is described); a product with personal context (Personal Intelligence), where the app supplies the details.
ядра.магнит_причина: Google examples in techniques/examples name concrete objects a generator could copy: ornate elven plate armor with falcon-wing pauldrons, siamese cat with a green left eye, golden retriever with aviator sunglasses, mushroom sprite.

ядра.ядро_en: Even short prompts will generate high-quality images, but you can take better control of the output by adding details bit-by-bit; while simple prompts still work, achieving professional results requires more specific instructions.

оговорки.текст_en: Google blogs: 'You can get great results with Gemini from simple one or two-sentence inputs'; for 'truly incredible images and more nuanced creative control' they point to the detailed guide.

In products, generation is presented as 'from a simple text description' (Gemini app, Slides) and 'a simple text prompt' (AI Overviews in Search); in Slides more control comes from 'Help me visualize' with a more detailed prompt, while 'Beautify this slide' works with no prompt at all.
The Personal Intelligence page contrasts long and short prompts only when personal context is connected; it does not claim that short prompts are better in general.

The AI Mode prompts shown by Google are unpolished (lowercase starts, typos 'an detailed', 'physicals') and are presented as having produced the shown result; the page does not claim that typos have no effect.
For Gemini 2.0 Flash (experimental, predecessor) the example prompt is a conversational request 'Hi, can you create a 3d rendered image of …?'.

The pages use these minimal prompts in code and agent demos ("Generate an image of a sunset over the ocean.", "Generate a cityscape for Kyoto"); calling them demos rather than quality samples is an extraction note, not a Google statement.

приёмы.текст_en: Workflow: start with a short prompt, add specifics (style, attribute, place, shot size) for control, then refine with short edit commands, relying on the chat memory.

Length by task (Pro examples): editing one property or requesting a format - 3-8 words; a new composition or a scene with several references - a long ordered description (shot, subjects, arrangement, light direction, background, atmosphere).
Most cookbook examples are 1-3 sentences: type/medium + subject + surroundings; style is set by specific visible features (outlines, palette, period markers) when it matters.
Add details gradually and keep experimenting ('Keep playing, experimenting, and iterating, until you get the image you want to use').

ядра.ядро_en: Describe the scene, don't just list keywords: a narrative, descriptive paragraph will almost always produce a better, more coherent image than a list of disconnected words; when starting from a blank canvas, you are the director and need to describe the scene narratively.

оговорки.текст_en: nb25 blog calls it "one fundamental principle"; the wording is cautious: "almost always".
nb2/pro guide frames it as directing: "stop typing keywords and start directing the scene" (to prompt like a creative director).
Mechanism given by Google: the model's core strength is deep language understanding that captures the nuance of prompts.
The six doc templates themselves are full descriptive sentences with slots, not keyword lists.
lite notebook examples: one or two full sentences followed by a comma-separated tail of style/technique descriptors ending with a plain background — see contradiction.

The Cloud guide (NB2/Pro) repeats the idea twice: 'you need to stop typing keywords and start directing the scene'; specificity comes through professional vocabulary: lighting, camera/lens, color grading/film stock, materials.

Think with Google (Pro, Asset Studio): 'Writing a great prompt requires both telling a succinct story and painting an elaborate tableau with words.' Aspect ratio is named as part of the prompt text (Asset Studio); the page says nothing about the API parameter.
All five comparison prompts on the NB2 Lite page are long narrative paragraphs (~150-200 words) without keyword lists, weights or parameters; the same prompts are used for NB2 and NB2 Lite.

When starting with a blank canvas, you are the director: a simple list of keywords won't cut it — you need to describe the scene narratively; writing a prompt is no longer just about keywords, it is about defining composition, lighting, aspect ratio, and emotional resonance.

приёмы.текст_en: Write each slot of the formula as its own sentence (the guide's example labels each sentence [Subject], [Action], [Location], [Composition], [Style]).
Narrative structure in NB2/Lite examples: shot type or genre frame -> subject and action -> composition -> surroundings with materials -> light -> palette -> final mood/artistic intent.

примеры.текст: [Subject] A striking fashion model wearing a tailored brown dress, sleek boots, and holding a structured handbag. [Action] Posing with a confident, statuesque stance, slightly turned. [Location/context] A seamless, deep cherry red studio backdrop. [Composition] Medium-full shot, center-framed. [Style] Fashion magazine style editorial, shot on medium-format analog film, pronounced grain, high saturation, cinematic lighting effect.
примеры.что_показывает_en: Text-to-image example following the formula with inline slot labels: a fashion model in a tailored brown dress (Subject), posing with a confident stance (Action), on a deep cherry red studio backdrop (Location), medium-full center-framed shot (Composition), fashion-editorial style on medium-format analog film with grain, high saturation and cinematic lighting (Style).

примеры.текст: A lone astronaut stands poised at the threshold of a futuristic corridor, their back to the viewer, gazing out towards a distant, mountainous landscape visible at the far end. The composition is perfectly symmetrical, using the clean, repeating lines of the brightly lit hallway to create a powerful vanishing point. The corridor itself is a marvel of sleek, sterile design, with glowing white panels on the walls and ceiling, and a highly reflective, cyan-tinted floor that mirrors the entire scene, doubling its visual impact. The astronaut, clad in a white and gold-trimmed spacesuit, is the central, human element in this otherwise impersonal, high-tech environment. The lighting is bright and even, giving the scene an ethereal, almost heavenly quality. The color palette is a minimalist blend of stark white, cool cyan, and the earthy tones of the distant planet. The artistic style is one of clean, utopian science fiction, evoking a sense of calm, wonder, and the beginning of a grand journey into the unknown.
примеры.что_показывает_en: Comparison prompt: a symmetrical sci-fi corridor scene with an astronaut seen from behind, detailing composition, materials, costume, lighting, palette and artistic style.

примеры.текст: From a breathtakingly high, top-down perspective, the image captures a dramatic, abstract view of a coastline. The composition is dynamically split by a diagonal slash of land and sea, running from the upper right to the lower left. On the left, a deep, inky navy-blue ocean churns into a brilliant white surf that resembles delicate, intricate lace or the marbled patterns in polished stone. The foam crashes against a narrow strip of pale, sandy beach, which gives way to shallow waters of stunning aquamarine and turquoise. The land itself, occupying the upper right corner, is a textured, rugged terrain of ochre, beige, and dark, earthy tones, appearing almost like a geological cross-section. The overall effect is less of a literal landscape and more of a powerful, painterly abstraction. The camera angle removes all sense of a horizon, transforming the familiar elements of water, sand, and rock into a sophisticated composition of color, texture, and dynamic, diagonal energy. The scene feels both immense in scale and microscopic in its fine detail, capturing a moment of powerful, natural artistry.
примеры.что_показывает_en: Comparison prompt: an abstract top-down aerial view of a coastline with a diagonal split, described through perspective, composition, colors, textures and the removal of the horizon.

примеры.текст: This cinematic, high-angle shot plunges the viewer directly into the action of soaring flight. A lone, dark bird, wings powerfully outstretched, glides with purpose through the center of the frame. The camera seems to be flying alongside it, capturing the majestic sweep of its wings against an epic backdrop. Below, a deep valley is completely choked with a sea of roiling white mist, swirling and shifting as if it were a living, breathing entity. The action is layered: the bird’s determined forward motion contrasts with the slow, churning chaos of the fog beneath it. Emerging from the mist, the dark, skeletal tips of a vast pine forest reach up like grasping hands. The entire scene is framed by the dark silhouettes of trees in the immediate foreground, creating a sense of vertigo and placing the viewer precariously on a high precipice, witnessing this primal scene unfold. The dramatic monochrome palette and sophisticated composition transform a simple act of flight into a thrilling, atmospheric event—a journey through a mysterious, untamed world where the only certainties are the driving beat of wings and the swirling abyss below.
примеры.что_показывает_en: Comparison prompt: a cinematic high-angle monochrome shot of a bird flying over a mist-filled pine valley, with camera movement, layered action, foreground framing and palette specified.

примеры.текст: A perfect, clear glass sphere rests on a rippling water surface, captured in an artistic macro photograph. The composition is compellingly off-center, with the sphere placed to the left, its weight creating concentric circles that spread across the dark, reflective water. Inside the sphere, a miniature, dreamlike world is refracted and inverted: a swirling vortex of fiery orange and brilliant gold light, resembling a sunset galaxy or a city street blurred into a whirlwind of motion. The camera angle is extremely low, almost at water level, which exaggerates the sphere’s presence and the intricate patterns of the ripples. The lighting is dramatic and high-contrast; the background is dark, punctuated by soft, out-of-focus orbs of blue and orange light—a classic bokeh effect—that suggest a city at night. This gives the scene a cinematic and mysterious atmosphere. The sophistication lies in the masterful control of light, reflection, and refraction, turning a simple object into a vessel holding a tiny, dynamic universe, creating a profound sense of wonder and technical artistry.
примеры.что_показывает_en: Comparison prompt: an artistic macro photograph of a glass sphere on rippling water, specifying off-center composition, refraction content, extremely low camera angle, high-contrast lighting and bokeh.

примеры.текст: In a breathtaking display of surreal transformation, a cinematic moment of pure action unfolds against a textured, golden-brown canvas. From the right, a woman is seen in elegant profile, her lips a startling slash of red. Her quiet composure is violently contradicted by the explosive event taking place: her dark hair is erupting, bursting forth into a chaotic flock of black birds. These creatures are captured mid-flight, a dynamic swarm launching from her mind and sweeping across the frame to the left. The motion is palpable; you can almost hear the frantic beating of a hundred wings as they break free. Some birds are still tangled, emerging from the dark mass of her hair, while others are already soaring into the open space. This is not a gentle release, but a powerful, almost violent, act of creation or liberation. The camera captures this impossible metamorphosis head-on, focusing on the sheer force of the birds' exodus. This highly sophisticated image is a kinetic masterpiece, portraying an internal storm made external, a thought process so intense it literally takes flight in a beautiful, dark, and unstoppable flurry of action.
примеры.что_показывает_en: Comparison prompt: a surreal profile of a woman whose hair bursts into a flock of black birds against a golden-brown textured background, with motion and camera framing described.

ядра.ситуация_в_промпте: The prompt is assembled as a comma-separated list of words ('girl, forest, sunset, 4k, cinematic') or as a set of tags. / A from-scratch generation prompt (no references) is written as a set of words or comma-separated tags; the task requires an expressive, directed scene.
ядра.не_применяется_когда: Short edit commands on an attached image ('Translate to French') and service lines (format, background) - they do not need to be written as narrative. / A short edit command on a finished image; product fields (NotebookLM, Photos templates) where the prompt is a setting; generation from references, where the key is the role of each reference.
ядра.магнит_причина: Negative instruction in the core ("don't just list keywords"; "a simple list of keywords won't cut it"); Google example prompts name concrete subjects a generator could copy (fashion model in a tailored brown dress, lone astronaut in a futuristic corridor, glass sphere on rippling water).

ядра.ядро_en: To achieve the best results and have more nuanced creative control, include the following elements in your prompt: Subject, Composition, Action, Location, Style, and (for edits) Editing instructions.

части.текст_en: Subject: Who or what is in the image? Be specific. (e.g., a stoic robot barista with glowing blue optics; a fluffy calico cat wearing a tiny wizard hat).
Composition: How is the shot framed? (e.g., extreme close-up, wide shot, low angle shot, portrait).
Action: What is happening? (e.g., brewing a cup of coffee, casting a magical spell, mid-stride running through a field).
Location: Where does the scene take place? (e.g., a futuristic cafe on Mars, a cluttered alchemist's library, a sun-drenched meadow at golden hour).
Style: What is the overall aesthetic? (e.g., 3D animation, film noir, watercolor painting, photorealistic, 1990s product photography).
Editing instructions (for edits) — listed among the elements to include in the prompt.

оговорки.текст_en: The DeepMind guide (rank 1) gives five construction components - Style, Subject, Setting, Action, Composition - in the form of questions; Subject is expanded: who/what, what it looks like, what it wears, how it stands.
The nb25 blog (2025-08-26) - 'consider including' six elements, no order prescribed; the Pro blog (2025-11-20) - 'include the following elements'.
Gemini Apps help: the subject, what it is doing, the background or surroundings + describe the style separately (photorealistic, charcoal drawing, watercolor painting, cartoon illustration).
Docs help adds the distance to the subject and materials: 'For better results, consider the subject, setting, distance to subject, materials, or background.'
Time of day and light in the examples are written into the location ('a sun-drenched meadow at golden hour').
The same five components serve as edit axes: rethink the style, change the character, swap the setting, alter the action, adjust the composition - one changes, the rest are preserved.
pro blog, beyond the basics: "Composition and aspect ratio: Define the canvas. (e.g., "A 9:16 vertical poster," "A cinematic 21:9 wide shot.")" and factual constraints for diagrams.
nb2 ADK codelab (agent system prompt): "The image generation prompt should include: Subject, environment, style, lighting, color and mood."
DeepMind model pages (pro/nb2/family): "Think about what you want to see – the characters, the setting, and the overall feel."

Location can carry time of day and light ("a sun-drenched meadow at golden hour"); Style can be a medium, genre or era ("3D animation, film noir, watercolor painting, photorealistic, 1990s product photography").

примеры.текст: "A close up of a boat made out of wood on a lake surrounded by trees at sunrise."
примеры.что_показывает_en: Example prompt illustrating the tip: "A close up of a boat made out of wood on a lake surrounded by trees at sunrise."

ядра.ситуация_в_промпте: A from-scratch generation prompt is being written and its completeness must be checked: is the subject named with features, what it does, where, how the shot is framed, in which style/medium; for an edit - is there an instruction on what exactly to change. / A full prompt is being assembled and it must be checked that all key elements are named (who, what they do, where, how it is shot, in which style).
ядра.не_применяется_когда: An information image (infographic, diagram), where the format and content are key; an edit of one property; generation from a simple concept relying on the model's reasoning. / A short edit on an attached image, where the image itself provides the rest of the context.
ядра.магнит_причина: Parts quote concrete Google example subjects a generator could copy (stoic robot barista with glowing blue optics, fluffy calico cat in a tiny wizard hat, futuristic cafe on Mars, cluttered alchemist's library).

термины.значение_en: who or what is in the shot; 'be specific': a noun + distinguishing features
how the shot is framed: shot size and angle (extreme close-up, wide shot, low angle shot, portrait)
what is happening in the shot
where the scene takes place; time of day/light is often included here
medium (illustration, photo, watercolor) + aesthetics (realism, retro-futurism, abstraction)
the edit instruction - the sixth element, for editing
framing: extreme close-up, wide shot, low angle shot, portrait (p.155)
overall aesthetics: medium, genre or era (p.155)

ядра.ядро_en: To get the most relevant results in the Gemini app and NotebookLM, try to always include: Persona (Who is Gemini acting as?), Task (What exactly do you need done?), Context (What details or documents should it use?), and Format (Do you want a table, bullet points, an email, or something else?).

части.текст_en: Persona: Who is Gemini acting as?
Task: What exactly do you need done?
Context: What details or documents should it use?
Format: Do you want a table, bullet points, an email, or something else?

оговорки.текст_en: The advice is general for the Gemini app and NotebookLM; the page does not tie it to image generation - for images it is only a hypothesis.
The example labels its parts with [Persona] [Task] [Context] [Format] after each sentence; the example is textual.

примеры.текст:
You are a professional business analyst.
[Persona]
Summarize the main action items from this week’s project updates.
[Task]
Focus on items that require immediate attention from leadership.
[Context]
Provide the response as a three-bullet executive summary.
[Format]

ядра.ядро_en: When generating an image from text alone (no reference images), you are the director and need to describe the scene narratively, using the formula: [Subject] + [Action] + [Location/context] + [Composition] + [Style].

части.текст_en: When generating an image, your prompt structure depends entirely on whether you are using reference images or relying solely on text.
When starting with a blank canvas, you are the director. A simple list of keywords won't cut it; you need to describe the scene narratively.
Formula: [Subject] + [Action] + [Location/context] + [Composition] + [Style]

оговорки.текст_en: Google's worked example - five sentences strictly in formula order, each with a slot label in brackets; style is set by genre + medium (film stock) + grain, saturation and light.
The page does not say whether to keep the '[Subject]'-style labels in a real prompt.
"When generating an image, your prompt structure depends entirely on whether you are using reference images or relying solely on text" — with references use the reference formula.
In the guide's example each slot is a separate sentence labelled inline ([Subject] … [Style] …); the page does not say whether the labels should stay in a real prompt.
In the example the [Style] slot carries medium/film, grain, saturation and lighting ("fashion-editorial style on medium-format analog film … cinematic lighting").

примеры.текст: [Subject] A striking fashion model wearing a tailored brown dress, sleek boots, and holding a structured handbag. [Action] Posing with a confident, statuesque stance, slightly turned. [Location/context] A seamless, deep cherry red studio backdrop. [Composition] Medium-full shot, center-framed. [Style] Fashion magazine style editorial, shot on medium-format analog film, pronounced grain, high saturation, cinematic lighting effect.
примеры.что_показывает_en: Example text-to-image prompt following the five-slot formula with slot labels inline (fashion model editorial).

ядра.ситуация_в_промпте: Generation from scratch from text only, with no references; the wishes in the task are scattered and need to be put in order: who, what they do, where, how the shot is framed, in which style. / An image from scratch from text alone, without references; no key element should be forgotten.
ядра.не_применяется_когда: There are reference images (the formula with reference roles); an image based on current data (the web search formula); editing a finished image. / There are reference images (a different formula) or the task is editing a finished image.
ядра.магнит_причина: Negation in the parts ("A simple list of keywords won't cut it"); the Google worked example names concrete subjects a generator could copy (striking fashion model in a tailored brown dress, sleek boots, structured handbag).

ядра.ядро_en: For multimodal (reference-based) generation, use the formula: [Reference images] + [Relationship instruction] + [New scenario].

части.текст_en: When generating an image, your prompt structure depends entirely on whether you are using reference images or relying solely on text.
Formula: [Reference images] + [Relationship instruction] + [New scenario]

Using the attached napkin sketch as the structure and the attached fabric sample as the texture [References], transform this into a high-fidelity 3D armchair render [Relationship]. Place it in a sun-drenched, minimalist living room [New Scenario].

оговорки.текст_en: The key slot is the Relationship instruction: each attachment is assigned a role ('as the structure', 'as the texture'), then the operation verb ('transform this into …') and, in a separate sentence, the new scene.
For a later combination the nb25 blog generates the subject and the surroundings with separate prompts (subject only; place only).
Give each reference its role in words ("Using the attached napkin sketch as the structure and the attached fabric sample as the texture") — references are told apart without numbers.
The formula comes from a guide based on weeks of testing Nano Banana 2 and Nano Banana Pro, so it is not restricted to one of the two.

примеры.текст: Using the attached napkin sketch as the structure and the attached fabric sample as the texture [References], transform this into a high-fidelity 3D armchair render [Relationship]. Place it in a sun-drenched, minimalist living room [New Scenario].
примеры.что_показывает_en: Example reference-based prompt assigning a role to each attached image (sketch = structure, fabric = texture), then transforming and placing the result.

ядра.ситуация_в_промпте: Reference images are attached to the task (sketch, material sample, photo of a product or a person), from which a new scene must be assembled. / Reference images are attached to the request (sketch, fabric sample, character), and a new scene must be assembled from them.
ядра.не_применяется_когда: No references; editing one uploaded image, where describing the change is enough. / Generation without references or a targeted edit of one image.
ядра.магнит_причина: Google example prompts name concrete subjects a generator could copy: napkin sketch and fabric sample turned into a 3D armchair in a sun-drenched living room, astronaut in a helmet, overgrown basketball court in the rainforest.

Relative dates are left for search to resolve ("last night's Arsenal game in the Champion's League").
Real-time data can drive a stylised scene (current weather integrated into an isometric city scene with a title/date/temperature block).

ядра.ядро_en: Across Google's generation templates and gallery prompts, the prompt opens with the image type / medium / style or shot type before the subject (e.g. "A photorealistic [type of shot] of…", "A [style] of…", "A high-resolution, studio-lit product photograph of…", "A photo of…"), then setting, lighting and camera, with the aspect ratio last where present.

модели_различия.текст_en: Imagen 3 examples put the explicit style/medium label at the start or at the end of the prompt.

оговорки.текст_en: Operation prompts (edit, search, transform) open with a verb instead ("Generate", "Change").
nb25 recipes: longer prompts go task/operation statement → concrete scene details → final sentence constraining the output (canvas/aspect, naturalness, output-only).

Pro and nb2 blogs: long prompts go shot/view → subjects and arrangement → setting → lighting with direction and sources → colours/background → atmosphere or format ("16:9 aspect ratio" / "AR: 16:9" at the very end).
Imagen 3 examples put the explicit style/medium label at the start or the end (other model).
No page states this order as a rule; it is the shared shape of templates and examples.
This is an observation from examples, not a rule formulated by Google.

Docs help: generation examples are single noun phrases without a verb following the scheme [mood/medium or view] of [subject with attributes/material] [setting/location] [background/depth] [time of day/light].
Sometimes the shot size/angle comes first ('A close up of …', 'A top-down view of …').
In the cookbook (Lite by default) the style, when it matters, is set by specific visible features after the type/medium + subject + surroundings sequence.

Google's generation examples typically open with the image type or medium, often with a style adjective, followed by the subject: 'A whimsical illustration of', 'A high-quality photo of', 'Generate a photorealistic picture of', 'A picture of', 'A photorealistic image of', 'Generate an image of'.

ядра.ядро_en: The key is to start a prompt with a strong verb that tells the model the primary operation you want to perform.

оговорки.текст_en: Observed: most notebook prompts begin with an imperative verb naming the operation (Create, Show me, Add, Move, Visualize, Make, Translate, Generate, Restore…); purely descriptive noun-phrase prompts are used mainly for plain generation.
Vertex docs examples open with an imperative verb and name the output type explicitly ("Generate an image of…", "Create a tutorial…").
Google Earth prompts are single imperative sentences starting with Render / Create / Reimagine / Add / Transform.
Gemini app edit examples open with a transformation verb aimed at the input ("Turn this photo into…", "Transform this house into…").
Gemini Apps help: 'Start your prompt with words like draw, generate, and create' - a signal of the intent 'an image is needed' in a chat interface; the help examples follow it.
Firebase: all example prompts open with an explicit verb ('Generate…', 'Create…', 'Edit this image…', 'Turn this…').

ядра.ядро_en: If you want images, clearly ask for images in your request — describe the intent with phrases such as "create an image of" or "generate an image of"; otherwise the multimodal model might respond with text instead of the image, and if the prompt is ambiguous it might create only text and no image (FinishReason NO_IMAGE).

части.текст_en: Prompt for images: Describe the intent by using phrases such as "create an image of" or "generate an image of".
The model might only generate text and no image (especially if the prompt is ambiguous). If this happens, the FinishReason is NO_IMAGE.
Try asking for image outputs explicitly. For example, "generate an image", "provide images as you go along", "update the image".

оговорки.текст_en: In Firebase the 'modalities' list (text-to-image, editing, etc.) is not a request field but recommended usage patterns; they are triggered by the prompt wording, while responseModalities is a separate parameter.

The common denominator of the limitations page: several failures are fixed by explicitly naming the needed modality - clearly ask for images, ask for text separately, first obtain the text that must appear in the image.

приёмы.текст_en: All Firebase examples open with an explicit verb and ask for an image directly.

примеры.что_показывает_en: Example wording to request images: "provide images as you go along."

ядра.не_применяется_когда: Product tools where image generation is set by a button (Docs 'Generate an image', Search 'Create image'); a purely text answer is needed.

ядра.ядро_en: Prioritize critical instructions: place essential behavioral constraints, role definitions (persona), and output format requirements in the System Instruction or at the very beginning of the user prompt; when providing large amounts of context, supply all the context first and place your specific instructions or questions at the very end, bridging with a clear transition phrase such as "Based on the information above...".

части.текст_en: Place essential behavioral constraints, role definitions (persona), and output format requirements in the System Instruction or at the very beginning of the user prompt.
When providing large amounts of context (e.g., documents, code), supply all the context first. Place your specific instructions or questions at the very end of the prompt.
After a large block of data, use a clear transition phrase to bridge the context and your query, such as "Based on the information above..."

оговорки.текст_en: The order of content can affect the answer; rearranging examples, context and input is itself an iteration technique.

ядра.ядро_en: Sequential art builds on character consistency and scene description to create panels for visual storytelling: "Make a 3 panel comic in a [style]. Put the character in a [type of scene]."

оговорки.текст_en: "the character" refers to the character from the input image.

Multi-panel layouts are named in the prompt by count or grid: "3x3 grid", "in four quadrants", "Triptych infographic", "Make 8 … logos … composition: a rendering of all logos on a single solid white background".

Opposite case: when a single image is wanted, the notebook says so explicitly ("It should be a single image, not a multi-tiled page", "no panels"); the first quote is a request to the text model that writes the prompts.
For accuracy with text and storytelling ability, these prompts work best with Gemini 3 Pro and Gemini 3.1 Flash Image.

ядра.ядро_en: To edit an image, give the model the image and describe the change you want in plain language (e.g., "Make the lighting darker.").

оговорки.текст_en: Google Earth: the on-screen view supplies the place; the prompt names only the transformation, referring to the place by name or "these/this".
Some edits are phrased as a creation request or a conversational question with possessives ("Create a picture of my cat…", "Can you transform this picture of mine…").
Longer consumer edits: first sentence = target transformation of the input, then separate sentences with specifics ("Include…", "Replace…", "Surround it with…").
The subject can be taken from the input by pointing and transformed by an era: "Create a photograph of the subject in this image as if they were living in the 1980s."
An edit differs from generation: a short imperative command referring to the source that describes only the change; a generation prompt describes the whole scene.
Edit prompts name the target (light, a specific object, background) and the new value (darker; a different colour and direction; specific colours).
Imagen inpainting: the mask sets where to edit, the prompt only what to do; Gemini 2.5 Flash Image: no mask, the model finds the object by its name itself.
Pro showcase edits are 3-5 words, only the change; preserving the rest is left to the model.
Several edits can be listed with commas in one request, addressing people by name (Google Photos).
Restoration: one can describe what is missing (nb25) or give a general command to restore the photo.
The edit axes coincide with the prompt construction components (style, character, setting, action, composition).
Named objects of the base prompt later become the addresses of local edits.

To edit, enter a prompt that describes how to adjust the image — describe the change you want in plain language (e.g., "Make the lighting darker."); instead of being limited to preset editing options, you can just type exactly what you want to see.

приёмы.текст_en: Refining edits - with short commands in the same chat, relying on the memory of the previous image.

Observed form of Google edit examples: they reference the attached image ("this image", "this photo", "these") and state only the target change with an imperative verb, without re-describing the scene; some examples do re-describe the scene.

оговорки.текст_en: When several geometric transformations are involved, it can be challenging to craft an imperative prompt; a descriptive prompt that directly describes the expected output ("upright", "filling the canvas") can be more straightforward.
An imperative prompt composes the scene in terms of actions — sometimes easier than writing descriptions.

Codelabs name the two styles ("imperative and descriptive prompts") without defining when to use which.
Three prompt forms are shown for the same editing task (imperative bullet list, declarative sentence(s), key-value list); the choice is tied to how easy the transformation is to describe.

ядра.ядро_en: Gemini excels at rendering text. Be clear about the text, the font style (descriptively), and the overall design.

оговорки.текст_en: pro page: "Describe what type of font you want, or simulate different types of handwriting."

Exact wording goes in quotation marks after a descriptor of the lettering ("Delicate script below reads: "…""); labels may be requested generically ("with a bold label"); unwanted text is excluded explicitly ("No text"); translation is a follow-up turn.
Letters can be built from objects, with the strength of the effect stated ("the resemblance to letters is subtle"); in logo prompts the words may be left to the model.
Per-line typography: position of each line + exact words in quotes + a named font, then an instruction to translate the text into other languages.

Greeting cards: card type + surface → design character → palette of three named colours → central graphic → first text in quotes + font → second message + font → card stock/finish → overall impression.
An observation across all text examples of the Pro announcement; this page does not state the quotes rule directly.

NB2/Pro ad example: text position ('Next to the product') + 'exact styling' line by line - the exact text in quotes, a description of the lettering and the font name; as the last step, translation of the text into other languages. The example uses single quotes.
The technique of text built into architecture comes with a caveat about the subtlety of the resemblance ('The houses still look like houses and the resemblance to letters is subtle').
To get a story in images without text, the India blog (nb25) says to explicitly not include words/text and to tell the story only through the image.
In-image labels (name, place, labels of key elements) are added in a separate phrase ('also add the name, location and label some key features').

Text-in-image prompts put the exact text in quotes ("BERLIN", "TYPOGRAPHY", the woodchuck phrase) and then specify letterform, colour, material or integration; when the model should choose the words, the prompt instead states a rule for them ("each is an expressive word").

ядра.ядро_en: Infographic examples name the format (isometric cutaway, triptych, flat lay DIY infographic, storybook infographic), enumerate the parts or labels to show (often quoted), state the style — sometimes as 'The style is <name>, characterized by…' — and give a palette; process topics encode order through direction or a connecting path ('left to right', 'then to… and finally').

оговорки.текст_en: State audience level and output language: "Make an infographic explaining Einstein's theory of General Relativity suitable for a 6th grader in Spanish".

"Include" + list of mandatory elements; the model composes the text itself.
Accuracy is not guaranteed — see the factual-accuracy core.

ядра.ядро_en: To generate text, specifically ask for text output (e.g., "generate narrative text along with illustrations") — the model may generate text as an image; Gemini can generate interleaved images with text in one response (e.g., images for each step of a generated recipe), and asking the model to generate both text and images for each step encourages interleaved output.

части.текст_en: The model may generate text as an image. Try asking for text outputs explicitly. For example, "generate narrative text along with illustrations".
You can use Gemini to generate interleaved images with text responses. For example, you can generate images for each step of a generated recipe without having to make separate requests to the model.
Generate an illustrated recipe for a paella. Create images to go alongside the text as you generate the recipe

оговорки.текст_en: The number of images is not guaranteed: 'The model might not create the exact number of images you ask for.'
Several images can be requested in one interaction for step-by-step instructions and visual stories.
Together with the image the model returns a text part that describes and complements what is generated.
"encourages" — raises the likelihood, not a guarantee.
Interleaving is requested in words ("interleave illustrations"); the Pro doc example has no separate parameter for it.
For mixed output the words ask for both results while response_format lists [text, image].
Per-image constraints can go into the step request: "generate each image in a 1:1 aspect ratio", "Label each image with the step number but no other words."
The model won't always follow the exact number of image outputs asked for.
Observation for Gemini 2.0 Flash (other, 2025-03): interleaved illustrated output was obtained by asking explicitly for an image per unit of content and enabling both modalities (Text + Image).

приёмы.текст_en: For multi-part output - an explicit scheme for each item (a title with the step number, an explanation, an image) and, if needed, the image format in words ('generate each image in a 1:1 aspect ratio').
For an illustrated story - ask for an image for each unit: 'For each scene, generate an image.'
Structure: task + exact number of steps → per-step structure (title with the number of the step, explanation, image) → image constraint.

ядра.ядро_en: Prompt engineering is iterative: these guidelines and templates are starting points — experiment and refine based on your specific use cases and observed model responses; if you're not getting the expected results, try rephrasing, and keep playing, experimenting, and iterating until you get the image you want to use.

оговорки.текст_en: Models are non-deterministic - a good result may take several attempts.
The general Gemini guide repeats iteration three times (intro note, strategies section, Gemini 3 template); for images by extension, while the DeepMind guide on Nano Banana says the same for images.
Thought summaries are available for thinking models (Gemini 3 and 2.5 series); image models are not named in that section.
The first scene "will have a cascading effect that defines the overall look of our story".

приёмы.текст_en: Different words with the same meaning produce different answers - rephrase; if the model does not follow an instruction, give an instruction for an analogous task with the same result.
If generation stopped before finishing - retry or change the prompt.

Workflow based on Vertex examples: explicit image intent -> purpose and specifics -> exclusions phrased positively -> camera angle -> complex scene in layers -> then one small change per refining turn.
Docs: each Create produces several variants; evaluate, adjust the prompt, create again, choose.

Prompt design is a process of trial and error: spend time on the first scene and refine the prompt or run it a few times to get the preferred variation; for complex transformations, craft your prompts iteratively, going from the most difficult operation to the last details; analyze thought summaries to understand failures and improve prompts.

ядра.ситуация_в_промпте: The first result did not match expectations, and the author is about to either rewrite everything from scratch or give up. / The result is unstable or a complex edit does not work on the first try.
ядра.не_применяется_когда: The result already fits the task. / A one-off simple generation.

ядра.ядро_en: For complex scenes with many elements, break your prompt into steps.

оговорки.текст_en: Google's example builds layers from the background to the foreground and to the focal object; each sentence is one layer with a spatial indication and its own verb (create / add / place).
The restoration skill (NB2) also orders the edit in numbered steps: varnish correction -> removal of soot and dirt -> restoration of losses.

приёмы.текст_en: Step markers First / Then / Finally, each bound to a plane: background → foreground → object on object ("First, create a background of … Then, in the foreground, add … Finally, place …").

примеры.текст:
First, create a background of a serene, misty
forest at dawn. Then, in the foreground, add a moss-covered ancient stone altar.
Finally, place a single, glowing sword on top of the altar.

ядра.ядро_en: Break down prompts into components: instead of having many instructions in one prompt, create one prompt per instruction; for complex tasks that involve multiple sequential steps, make each step a prompt and chain the prompts so the output of one becomes the input of the next; or perform different parallel tasks on different portions of the data and aggregate the results.

части.текст_en: Instead of having many instructions in one prompt, create one prompt per instruction. You can choose which prompt to process based on the user's input.
For complex tasks that involve multiple sequential steps, make each step a prompt and chain the prompts together in a sequence.
Aggregation is when you want to perform different parallel tasks on different portions of the data and aggregate the results to produce the final output.

An audiobook (merged MP3 via the File API) can be the source.

Finally, perform a highly precise restoration and output the restored IMAGE. REQUIRED: In your response, return a text part summarizing your process and naming any skills used.
Please restore this image using the appropriate techniques. (followed by the image as a media part)
This application is bundled with three skills: drawings, paintings, and photography, as each distinct art style requires its own set of custom instructions.

оговорки.текст_en: SKILL.md for paintings: a description line (activation trigger), a minimal-intervention directive, three mandates (Absolute Fidelity, Anti-Modernization, Patina & Craquelure) and three numbered steps.

The post justifies the layers by token savings and model focus, not image quality; the skill is an early version and the result may take several attempts.

примеры.текст:
---
name: paintings
description: Restoration protocol for fine art paintings.
---

# Painting restoration

Perform direct, minimal-intervention restoration of fine art paintings. Prioritize historical integrity, original pigment depth, and surface textures over cosmetic modernization. Do not include any elements, nor introduce any techniques not present in the original piece.

### 1. Core conservation mandates
* **Absolute Fidelity:** Strictly forbidden to add new subjects, figures, scenery, details, or narrative elements under any circumstances.
* **Anti-Modernization:** Retain original brushstroke characteristics. Do not flatten support textures.
* **Patina & Craquelure:** Respect the natural crack network (craquelure) as part of the artwork's history. Do not fill or erase cracks unless they pose an active risk of paint loss.

### 2. Step-by-step restoration process
1. **Varnish Correction:** Gently balance aged, yellowed natural varnishes to recover original pigment chromaticity without forcing modern, high-contrast saturation.
2. **Soot & Grime Reduction:** Isolate and lift surface grime while protecting delicate, thin underlying glaze layers.
3. **Inpaint Major Loss:** Where paint layers are missing, use references from the surviving elements to bridge the gap. Replicate the original brush direction, speed, height, transparency, and light source.

ядра.ядро_en: Aspect ratio is specified in two ways without being reconciled: in the prompt text (templates end with "[Aspect ratio]"; "Aspect ratio 16:9.", "Square image.", "3:2 wallpaper", "A 9:16 vertical poster") and via the aspect_ratio parameter.

оговорки.текст_en: API doc: some examples use both, some only the text (mug and maple-leaf examples send "Square image." with no aspect_ratio parameter); the page does not say how the model treats text-only or mismatched ratios.
DeepMind Pro page and consumer blogs: the format is always written inside the prompt text, usually at the end; no separate parameter shown.
pro blog: "Composition and aspect ratio: Define the canvas."
Notebooks set the format in config, not in prompt words; the sprite example duplicates "square aspect ratio" in text and 1:1 in config.
ADK test prompt appends "16:9" directly to the text.
The Vertex page shows both ways (config '16:9' in REST and a phrase in the console example prompt) and does not say which wins in a conflict.
nb25 blog: the ratio is set only in the prompt text; the API parameter is not mentioned.
Gemini app FAQ (NB2): the ratio is written as text at the end of the prompt.
Asset Studio illustration: a short command 'change aspect ratio' without a target value produced three size variants.

You can prompt for desired dimensions: aspect ratio can be written as text in the prompt (e.g., 'with 2:3 aspect ratio', 'generate each image in a 1:1 aspect ratio') as well as set in the request config (imageConfig.aspectRatio).
The model struggles with maintaining aspect ratios — while you can prompt for desired dimensions, the output may not always support your requests.

ядра.ядро_en: With Personal Intelligence, instead of writing out the intricate details of your life, you can use simple prompts like "design my dream house"; Gemini pulls the right context from your connected Google apps (and your photos in Google Photos) and automatically fills in the blanks, grounding every creation in the things you care about most.

оговорки.текст_en: Previously a personal result required long detailed descriptions and manual upload of reference photos; Google names finding the right prompt as one of the main obstacles.
Works only in the Gemini app with Personal Intelligence connected (with Nano Banana 2 per the 2026-04-16 post); there is no such context in the API.
'grounding' here means relying on the user's personal context, not Google Search grounding.
The key to the mechanism is possessive words ('my', 'me and my family', 'our favorite'): they refer to the personal context.
A short personal prompt can be supplemented with composition in a second sentence ('We want to be standing in the center of the image, staring straight forward').
The page does not claim that short prompts are better in general - only when personal context is connected.

ядра.ядро_en: Coming up with your own prompt can be daunting, so Google Photos adds a Create with AI section featuring ready-made AI templates powered by Nano Banana — e.g., "put me in a high fashion photoshoot", "create a professional headshot", "put me in a winter holiday card" — plus personalized templates such as "create a name doodle personalized to me" and "create a cartoon of me and my hobbies".

оговорки.текст_en: Three levels of prompting in Photos: a free description of the edit/style ('Help me edit', 'Ask') -> ready-made templates -> personalized templates based on gallery data.
The template name is shorter than what it does (new background, props, a greeting inscription); the full template text is not disclosed.
All examples are short imperative phrases with a recognizable genre/format, usually with 'me' as the subject; light, camera and composition are not described - the genre name carries the style.

ядра.ядро_en: In NotebookLM (Gemini Notebook), input a prompt to describe the output you want to create from your sources — for an Infographic you can guide the style, color, or focus (e.g., "Use a blue color theme and highlight the 3 key stats."); Video Overviews take a free-text instruction alongside preset choices (format and visual style), Slide Decks take free-text prompts, and the content comes from the notebook sources.

оговорки.текст_en: Infographic: fixed parameters (language, level of detail, orientation, visual style) + a free prompt; the prompt used can be viewed via 'View custom prompt'.
Video Overviews (nb25): both free-text examples steer the content focus ('Focus only on …'), not the visual style; the presets are the format (Explainer/Brief) and one of six styles.
Slide Decks (Pro + creative agents): prompts are short, often fragments; some are only about content, some only about style, some mixed; several sources are named by role.

ядра.ядро_en: Handle multimodal inputs coherently: when using text, images, audio, or video, treat them as equal-class inputs and ensure your instructions clearly reference each modality as needed.

оговорки.текст_en: The rule comes from the general Gemini 3 guide; for images it is supported only by examples (extraction inferences), there is no direct wording on image pages.

приёмы.текст_en: Refer to the input by pointing rather than by retelling: 'this plant', 'this scene', 'these images', 'the dress in the image', 'the subject in this image'; the appearance of subjects from input photos is not described.
The nb25 notebook names the inputs explicitly and in the order of the request parts: 'the provided source image', 'the provided canvas', 'the first/second image', 'this image'.

Refining turns in a chain do not retell the appearance but refer ('that cat', 'it', 'this infographic') and name only the change; 'Now, center the omelet in the pan' refers to an object from the previous turn.
With several sources (NotebookLM) each is named by its role ('Use the brandbook for branding and styling references', 'Reference the recipe from the note').
In Docs, prompts point to the document content ('the dates in this document', 'the process described in this text') rather than retelling it.
In Slides/Vids the selected image is the input; the prompt names only the change and refers to the object by pointing ('this product').
India blog example pattern: transformation verb + pointer to the input ('this photo', 'these two protagonists') + goal, plus additions if needed.

ядра.примечание: Размерджено из Я-промптинг-48 по Л9 (проверка Я-промптинг-48#2): общий принцип Gemini 3 (E-271-26) — другое утверждение, чем индексы картинок; статус один_источник: прямая формулировка одна (E-271-26), остальное — примеры и выводы извлечения (Л2)

словарь_терминов.значение_en: what is unwanted is expressed by a positive description of the scene ('an empty, deserted street') rather than by the word 'no'. Variants across pages (part 1): on p.22 a 'negative prompt' is the opposite - a block of bans in text; on p.85 it is a separate Imagen field.

a list of what must not be in the image. Variants across pages (part 1): for Gemini Image it is text inside the prompt; for Imagen a separate field; the Gemini docs (p.1) advise a semantic positive wording instead.
a command prompt: describes actions to perform on the input
a prompt that describes the expected result. Variants across pages (part 1): p.80 uses both words as synonyms; p.76 (E-76-42) calls any descriptive generation prompt without a verb 'descriptive'.
a prompt written as 'key: value' lines (Task, Subject, Corrections, Background, Border, Position)
closed - specific instructions and constraints to control the output; open - fully creative mode
a generic word is replaced by a description of type, material, finish and shape details
the purpose of the image (segment, aesthetics, brand domain) as part of the prompt, from which the model infers the style (parts 1 and 2 agree).

the prompt element about how the shot is built: shot size, angle and framing. Variants across pages: p.155 and the Pro blog - framing (extreme close-up, wide shot, low angle shot, portrait); p.45 - shot size and centering; p.79 - the language of framing as opposed to graphics software terms; p.80 - margins/filling the canvas; p.137 - a 'composition:' label for layout and background; Think with Google - one of the elements the prompt defines together with lighting, aspect ratio and emotion.

the overall aesthetics of the image: medium + aesthetics. Variants across pages: p.155 - medium, genre or era; p.45 and the Cloud example - genre + medium (film stock) + grain/saturation/light; p.1 - 'artistic style' next to 'medium'; DeepMind - medium (illustration, photograph, watercolor) + aesthetics (realistic, retro-futuristic, abstract); Gemini Apps - photorealistic, charcoal drawing, watercolor painting, cartoon illustration.
the instruction on how the references relate to each other, what to take from each (the role of each reference) and how to combine them (parts 1 and 2 agree).

словарь_терминов.термин: Source/Search request · Analytical task · Visual translation
словарь_терминов.значение_en: the slots of the web-search formula: Source/Search request, Analytical task (how the retrieved data changes the scene) and Visual translation (the visual form into which the data is turned) (parts 1 and 2 agree).

grounding the answer/generation in external data or context. Variants across pages: p.9/45 and the Cloud guide - Google Search data, the model itself decides whether to search; p.133 - text grounding strictly on User Context (a different meaning, not taken into the cores); p.187 - relying on the user's personal context (Personal Intelligence), not Google Search grounding.
web image search as visual context for generation (search_types web_search + image_search, 3.1 Flash)
a response in which text and images alternate within one answer (parts 1 and 2 agree).
the model's reasoning level before rendering
summaries of the model's reasoning - a prompt debugging tool

developer instructions separate from the content: a preamble that sets the model's behavior before the user's instructions. Variants across pages: p.19/125 - an API field, text only; p.22 - the image model 'currently ignores' them, the rules are sent as a message and called 'system instructions'; p.98/99 - a channel for brand rules for text models.

a label 'image 1' / 'a' before the image that the text refers to. Variants across pages (part 1): p.88 - the label is placed BEFORE the image; p.79 - image roles listed at the start of the prompt; p.1 - ordinal words must match the order of the parts.
input images that set a character, an object, a style or a structure
a character sheet - an appearance reference
recognizability of a character/object from a reference. Variants across pages (part 1): p.165 extends it to 'identity and attire'.
a comic/storyboard made of panels
empty space in the frame (often for text)
a photo fills the whole frame without margins, so the composition is not specified for a 'photo'
the material, colour, texture and finish of a logo, product, character or object (parts 1 and 2 agree).
an accuracy requirement in the prompt + factually correct inputs (for diagrams) (parts 1 and 2 agree).

Gemini's knowledge of the world (real objects, places, eras and processes) used in generation. Variants across pages: for NB2 (p.165) - plus web search data and images; for Pro - 'connected to Google Search's vast knowledge base' (E-231-7); the Cloud guide separately describes real-time web search (E-317-40).
how strictly the model follows a complex prompt
the font is described in words (serif, bold, sans-serif). Variants across pages (part 1): p.45 (E-45-50) names typefaces in an example (Brush Script, Impact, Century Gothic).
composing a prompt for the needed answer. Variants across pages (part 1): p.127 - a process of trial and error; p.132 - 'authoring prompt and response pairs', mixed with a pretraining dataset.
refining an image in a dialogue in plain language
Imagen's LLM prompt rewriter, enabled by default. Variants across pages (part 1): for imagen-4.0-fast with a complex prompt it is advised to turn it off.
a reference number in the Imagen Customization prompt text; a subject description before the tag
the model's knowledge cutoff date; it is advised to state it explicitly
a model that reasons before answering; changes the way of prompting (conciseness). Variants across pages (part 1): stated for Gemini 3 in general; image models are not named.
the reason for blocking a prompt in promptFeedback
an edit where the place of the change is set by marks drawn over the image (parts 1 and 2 agree).
a generation pipeline based on prompts and assets, without fine-tuning
a text model response following a JSON schema (name + prompt)

the brand of Gemini image models. Variants across pages (part 2): on 2025 pages - Gemini 2.5 Flash Image (E-284-3, E-191-19); on p.317 (2026-03) 'Nano Banana models' = NB2 + Pro; 'our/the latest Nano Banana model' (p.203, 208) - without a version, p.203 by link = NB2 Lite; in the Pro blog (E-273-20) 'Built on Gemini 3 Pro, Nano Banana …' - the Pro name is shortened to 'Nano Banana'.

the family of Gemini image models. Variants across pages (part 2): Firebase (p.227): all - Pro, NB2, Lite (+ the deprecated 2.5); Cloud blog (p.317): NB2 and Pro; p.228: 'Gemini 3.x Image models' (Lite is not named on the page).

a prompt with specifics; gives more control and brings the result closer to what was imagined. Variants across pages (part 2): DeepMind - characters, setting, overall feel; Cloud blog - subject, lighting, composition; NB2 page - 'as many specifics as you can think of'; general Gemini 3 guide (E-271-23) - 'clearly and concisely'.

словарь_терминов.термин: Subject / Composition / Action / Location (Setting) / Style / Editing instructions
словарь_терминов.значение_en: the components of an image prompt. Variants across pages (part 2): the place is named differently: Location (blogs), Setting (DeepMind), Location/context (p.317), scene (p.213), background or setting (p.208). DeepMind - 5 components without Editing instructions; blogs - 6.
directing the scene through narrative versus a list of keywords

describe what you want, not what you don't want. Variants across pages (part 2): the positive Vertex example itself contains 'with no signs of traffic'; the general Gemini guide (E-271-3) allows 'what to do and not to do'.
the negative prompt field (Imagen). Variants across pages (part 2): not supported on Gemini Image; legacy on Imagen since imagen-3.0-generate-002.
the FinishReason when the model returned only text

in Firebase 'modalities' are recommended usage patterns; responseModalities is a call parameter. Variants across pages (part 2): one word with two meanings: a usage scenario (text-to-image, editing) versus the TEXT/IMAGE parameter in the request.

the role the model acts as. Variants across pages (part 2): in the Workspace guide - the first element of the prompt (Persona/Task/Context/Format); in the Gemini 3 guide and the Genkit example - part of the system instruction.
a prompt with examples of the correct answer
a Gemini-improved version of the prompt using the template 'Make this a power prompt: …'

a verb for the primary operation at the start of the prompt. Variants across pages (part 2): Gemini Apps - draw/generate/create; Cloud guide - an operation verb (Remove, Using … transform, Search for).
detailed prompts and high-quality references as a condition for a high-quality result
the subject matter of the image / its aesthetic execution
a condensed story + an elaborate verbal picture

aspect ratio. Variants across pages (part 2): Think with Google and the nb25 blog - an element of the prompt text; Vertex - both the imageConfig.aspectRatio parameter and a phrase in the prompt, priority not stated.
image generation as a property of Gemini itself
personal context from connected Google apps and Google Photos

the user's free text for a product feature. Variants across pages (part 2): NotebookLM - a prompt for a Studio output, visible via 'View custom prompt'; Slides/Vids - a free image edit prompt instead of presets.
ready-made edit templates in Google Photos
a prompt starter in the interface with a slot. Variants across pages (part 2): the starter 'Swap [object] with…', the example - 'Swap … for …'.
a multi-model pipeline: a text model writes a structured script, the image model draws
a file of instructions for a task type, loaded on demand. Variants across pages (part 2): in the Google course (p.225) 'skills' are the course's skill badges - a different meaning.
an explanatory image: infographic, diagram, technical breakdown
about 4 characters; 100 tokens are about 60-80 English words
restricting the edit area (p.1)
a hand-drawn summary infographic (sketchnote) (p.106)
fine-tuning a model for a specialized task
cycle: model selection -> prompt engineering -> tuning -> optimization -> deployment -> monitoring
the required text prompt field of Imagen (p.120)

вопросы.текст: Соотношение сторон в API: учитывает ли модель формат, написанный только в тексте промпта («Square image.»), и что побеждает при расхождении текста и параметра aspect_ratio — ни одна страница части не говорит (Я-промптинг-1-45 (=Я-промптинг-82)). [то же в ч2: Что побеждает при конфликте: соотношение сторон словами в промпте или imageConfig.aspectRatio? Страница показывает оба способа (E-282-21).]

Правило «semantic negative» против явных «No text»/«no other words» в официальных примерах Google: при конвертации в правило завода нужно решение, считать ли исключение текста допустимым исключением (Я-промптинг-1-9 (=Я-промптинг-36), магнит).
вопросы.чем_снят: правка: Л11 — правило «describe what you want» (Я-промптинг-36) — рекомендация с магнитом; ядро-факт о коротких исключениях — Я-текст-12 (Б-1), связь «уточняет»

вопросы.текст: Стр.150 (2025-12-29): «Nano Banana» без версии разрешено в nb25 по правилу даты, хотя Nano Banana Pro вышел 2025-11-20 и тренды 2025 могли включать Pro — подтвердить правило.
вопросы.чем_снят: правка: Л1 — стр.150 называет и Nano Banana Pro, правило даты неприменимо (ТЗ_СВЕДЕНИЕ) → не_указано

вопросы.текст: Стр.45 (гайд Cloud Blog, 2026-03-05): «не указано» разрешено в nb2+pro по чужой странице (E-110-5: гайд тестировал NB2 и Pro) — допустим ли такой признак.
вопросы.чем_снят: Снят сшивкой: ч2 разрешила ту же статью Cloud Blog (стр.317 — копия стр.45 с параметром ?e=) в nb2+pro по прямому указанию самой страницы: обобщённые имена «Gemini Image models»/«Nano Banana» на ней относятся к Nano Banana 2 и Nano Banana Pro (см. разрешение_моделей ч2). Признак по чужой странице (E-110-5) больше не нужен.

вопросы.текст: Стр.79/80: «не указано» разрешено по модели ноутбука, названной на той же странице (lite / nb25) — подтвердить.
вопросы.чем_снят: правка: Л1 — стр.80: gemini-2.5-flash-image лишь модель по умолчанию из трёх → не_указано; стр.79: ноутбук на одной модели gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image → lite (идентификатор модели в коде)

вопросы.текст: Краткость Gemini 3 (E-6-22, E-133-51): страницы не говорят, относится ли совет к image-моделям; сейчас разнесено по моделям (текстовые Gemini 3 против Gemini Image).
вопросы.чем_снят: правка: Л1 — Я-промптинг-33: pro/nb2/lite → не_сказано, для image-моделей в модели_различия — правило детальности

вопросы.текст: «The model currently ignores system instructions» (E-22-25) — состояние на дату ноутбука (копирайт 2026, дата не указана); актуально ли для NB2/Pro сейчас — в части нет подтверждения.
вопросы.чем_снят: Частично: для Pro карточка gemini-3-pro-image (E-261-7, ранг 1, 2026-09-22, ядро ч2 Я-промптинг-2-39) указывает «System instructions Supported»; для NB2/Lite подтверждения нет. Ядра не слиты, связь «конфликтует», противоречие записано по правилу (а).

вопросы.текст: Метки слотов формул ([Subject] … [Style]) в примерах стр.45: оставлять ли их в настоящем промпте — страница не говорит (E-45-66). [то же в ч2: Оставлять ли в реальном промпте метки слотов '[Subject]', '[Action]' и т.п.? Cloud-гайд держит их в разобранных примерах, но не говорит (E-317-66).]
Индексы картинок «image 1 / a» (E-88-50, r1) взяты со страницы понимания изображений (текстовая модель); для генерации подтверждение только из ноутбука r2 (E-79-30).
вопросы.чем_снят: правка: Л1 — Я-промптинг-48: индексы подтверждены для lite и не_указано; для pro/nb2/nb25 адресация по содержанию/ролям записана в модели_различия

вопросы.текст: Стр.38 (ai.google/prompts, ранг 5) взята в ядро «снятие ассоциации отрицанием» как пример; официальность ранга 5 — на усмотрение шва.
Шов с частью 2: ядра детальности, позитивной формулировки, текста в кадре, референсов, правки, вероятно, продолжаются в ч.2 — сшивать по подтемам и кодам лучших источников.
вопросы.чем_снят: Снят сшивкой: ядра обеих частей сведены (28 слияний, см. «слито»), в т.ч. детальность, позитивная формулировка, текст в кадре, референсы, правка.

вопросы.текст: Глагол первым (E-317-25, E-208-40) или субъект/тип изображения первым (E-317-28/29, E-209-36, E-304-43) для генерации с нуля — нужен прямой замер или официальное уточнение.
вопросы.чем_снят: правка: Л12 — обязательного порядка Google не задаёт; «тип кадра/медиум первым» — наблюдение (Я-промптинг-22, выведено), глагол первым — правило E-45-25 (Я-промптинг-23)

вопросы.текст: Список 15 языков лучшего качества для NB2 и Lite есть только в Firebase (ранг 4, E-227-63); Vertex (ранг 1, E-345-2) называет только Gemini 3 Pro Image — подтвердить для NB2/Lite.

вопросы.текст: У 22 ядер есть противоречия, решённые по правилам а–ж (Я-промптинг-1, 4, 6, 7, 13, 18, 22, 23, 33, 34, 36, 40, 42, 44, 47, 48, 52, 58, 78, 82, 84, 87), но статус у всех «согласовано», ни одного «решено_по_правилу». ТЗ_СВЕДЕНИЕ перечисляет «решено_по_правилу» отдельным статусом; это отступление решениями координатора не покрыто. Нужна единая линия.

Значение «да» у модели (общие сомнения п.1): в промптинге у 26 ядер «да» поставлено по примерам другой формы, по оговоркам с другим утверждением или по версиям противоречий, которые сами решены «другая модель/задача» (см. проблемы вида «модели»). Правило координатора («да» = утверждение ядра относится к модели) такие случаи не покрывает; нужна линия: считать ли пример/оговорку основанием для «да».

Vertex: в промпте «each image in a 1:1 aspect ratio», в REST на той же странице imageConfig.aspectRatio «16:9»
Cookbook: формат задаётся параметром, не словами
A2UI codelab: 1K/2K/4K и 1:1/16:9/9:16 передаются только текстом, imageConfig не передаётся

сводка:
Шаг 4б (правки по проверке и проходу поперёк): 98 → 99 ядер — Я-промптинг-48 размерджено по Л9 (индексы картинок остались в 48, общий принцип Gemini 3 о ссылках на входы вернулся ядром Я-промптинг-99); ядер в не_сведено по Л2 не убрано (Я-промптинг-50 — пример правила Я-рефы-41 — оставлено «выведено» из-за группы дублей 200).
Модели пересчитаны по Л1: «да» только по формулирующей единице с явным признаком модели; 75 ячеек «да» → «не_сказано» (пример, оговорка, сторона противоречия, модель по умолчанию в ноутбуке стр.20/22/80/326, стр.150/276 с Pro); где отличие по модели подтверждено кодами — записано в модели_различия; у ядер с nb25 = «да» пометка о снятии gemini-2.5-flash-image 02.10.2026.
Статусы: выведено 9 (Л2/Л12: 12, 20, 22, 37, 50, 53, 70, 72, 97), один_источник 13 (Л6: копии 45=317, 155=273, 258=306 и ядра на одной прямой единице), решено_по_правилу 1 (Я-промптинг-78: system instructions разнесены по платформам, Л5), спор 1 (Я-промптинг-82: формат словами против параметра, С-24, живой замер); Imagen (87–89) — действует: false по Л3.
Формулы со слотами, которых у Google нет (20, 70, 71, 72, 97), переведены в правило_промпта без придуманных слотов, дословные промпты — в примерах; скелет шаблонов Imagen (88) — в приём с выведено=true; частично подтверждённые 16, 50, 58, 89 сужены по Л15, 40 — до прямых слов Google.
Сила по Л4 (must → требование у 5, can/could → возможность у 10, 40, 48, 67, 71, 75, 81; «требование» без слов Google у 88 снято); класс по Л17 (80, 81 → возможность_модели), 47 → процедура.
Магниты пересмотрены по Л7: 65 true (конкретные предметы примеров, запреты и отрицания в порождающей позиции), 66 → false; шумные причины сшивки переписаны.
Слой (Л14): промпт 80, инструкция 9, справка 10; дом (Л10): 33 ядра живут в других темах (связь «уточняет» на домашнее ядро), 11 — дома групп в промптинге; межтемные связи переведены на новые коды.
Сомнения: Я-промптинг-78 решено по платформам вопреки «остаётся спор» реестра С-34; Я-промптинг-46 — вместо «выведено» один_источник после возврата прямой E-177-2; nb2 у шаблонов доков оставлено по подписи примера (вопрос).

методика.модели: ключи pro/nb2/lite/nb25/other/не_указано; строки с «по умолчанию X» → только X; «не указано» разрешено только для стр.45, 79, 80, 150 (причина — в source.модель_разрешена и ядро.модели_разрешение)
методика.дата: дата_ед, иначе ISO из дата_стр; для стр.45/155/163/166/167 дата из текста страницы; копирайт-год без даты → null
методика.лучший_источник: среди ядро_коды (единицы, выражающие само утверждение): минимальный ранг → самая свежая дата → прямо полученная раньше выведенной → вид (правило>инструкция>ограничение>предупреждение>шаблон>приём>факт>объяснение>пример); одно ручное исключение помечено
методика.сила: как у лучшего источника; при «гайд-против-примера» не выше «рекомендация»
методика.фрагмент: цитата единицы (до 160 знаков); у выведенных единиц — «[выведено: …]» + начало утверждения

ключи_моделей.other: не-Nano-Banana модели: Gemini 2.0 Flash image, Imagen, Veo, текстовые Gemini
ключи_моделей.не_указано: модель на странице не названа и не разрешается явным признаком
